## Background

The [Scientific American](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/why-are-we-getting-taller/) argues that humans have been getting taller over the years. As the data scientists that we are becoming, we would like to find data that validates this concept.

This project is not as severe as the two quotes below, but it will give you a taste of pulling various data and file formats together into "tidy" data for visualization and analysis.

> "Classroom data are like teddy bears and real data are like a grizzly bear with salmon blood dripping out its mouth." [Jenny Bryan](https://twitter.com/JennyBryan)

> "Up to 80% of data analysis is spent on the process of cleaning and preparing data" Hadley Wickham

## Pre

1.  Read in and tidy the [Worldwide heights estimates .xlsx file](https://byuistats.github.io/M335/data/heights/Height.xlsx)
    -   Make sure the file is in long format with year as a column. See [Example of the Tidy Excel File after formatting](https://byuistats.github.io/M335/maleheight_tidy.html)
    -   Use the `separate()` and `mutate()` functions to create a decade column.
2.  To check your work and verify there are no data issues, make a plot with decade on the x-axis and and all the countries heights in inches on the y-axis; with the points from Germany highlighted based on the data from the `.xlsx` file.
    -   Don't worry about formatting and labelling the plot too much at this point. You will do that as part of the *post class* task.
3.  Knit the `.Rmd` file. Push your `.Rmd`, `.md`, and `.html` files into your GitHub repository.

## Post

1.  Fix whatever issues you discovered in your data/plot by sharing with others in class.
2.  Improve the visualization. Take time to fine tune the formatting and labelling.
3.  Write a paragraph to summarize how you would respond to the assertion that humans are getting taller over the years. (Does your data tell a story?)
4.  Knit the `.Rmd` file. Push your `.Rmd`, `.md`, and `.html` files into your GitHub repository.

### Submit

In I-learn submit a link to the `.md` file on GitHub.
